summary: Unexpected model pin reset during regional canary expansion due to health-probe header rewrite
description:
Issue summary:
During a staged canary expansion for Finlytics (enterprise tenant) traffic was unexpectedly routed to the degraded fallback variant (opt-7B-quant) despite the tenant having an explicit model pin set to open-7B-v2. Impact: user-facing quality regressions and a short billing spike due to heavier quantized variant usage.

Impact:
- Several hundred requests observed returning lower-quality responses for ~18 minutes for sessions that had previously been pinned.
- Customer reported multiple production incidents and opened a support call.

Environment:
- Prod, us-east primary; canary slice expanding to eu-west.
- Dedicated capacity pool (enterprise).

Steps to reproduce (observed):
1) Tenant has an active explicit pin to redwood/open-7B-v2 (cookie+X-Model-Pin header in Client).
2) Canary expansion triggered across regions; sidecar health probes roll out to new edge proxies.
3) Upstream edge proxy rewrites health probe headers (strip/normalize custom headers) causing the orchestration layer to see the cohort as unhealthy during probe handshake.
4) Router triggers fallback routing policy which prefers a compatible quantized variant to keep latency SLOs.
5) Subsequent requests for pinned sessions are served by fallback variant until pin is re-established.

Observed logs / snippets:
- edge-proxy: "probe-received: client_id=finlytics-42 probe_id=hk-7; headers=[Host, User-Agent, Accept]"
- router: "pin-check: cookie present=true header:X-Model-Pin missing=false decision=ROUTE_TO_FALLBACK reason=probe-unhealthy"
- control-plane: "cohort-health: us-east->eu-west: snapshot-mismatch: 18s"

Notes: the edge proxy rewrote the probe exchange such that the X-Model-Pin header did not correlate to the shard health window, producing transient pin loss at the routing layer.
steps_to_reproduce: Tenant with explicit pin pinned to open-7B-v2
Observe edge health probe rewrite in edge logs
Watch router decisions revert sessions to fallback variant
comments: 2026-03-12 10:22 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer alerted via phone about QPS shift and quality regression. Attached request ids and sample transcripts.

2026-03-12 10:45 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Initial triage — observed cohort-health anomaly coincident with canary expansion window. Raised hypothesis that health-probe normalization may be stripping custom pin header.
2026-03-12 11:10 - Priya Natarajan (Control Plane Eng): Confirmed router decision logs showing probe-unhealthy path. Added instrumentation flag to log incoming header sets for suspect probes.

2026-03-13 02:30 - Diego Alvarez (SRE): Deployed temporary rule to preserve X-Model-Pin on probe flows and kicked a targeted reassert of pin for affected tenant. Customer confirmed improvement; quality metrics returned to baseline.
2026-03-14 09:00 - Maya Chen (Support): Customer requested permanent mitigation and follow-up postmortem.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Edge health probe normalization strips or rewrites custom headers causing control plane to evaluate cohort as unhealthy — confirmed by header audit logs.

Hypothesis 2: Pin TTL (default 30s) is too short for cross-region canary probe window; combinatorial effect with probe rewrite creates gap — observed pins expiring while control plane awaiting health confirmation.
Logs show a narrow window (~12-22s) where router lacked consistent pin info for specific session cookies leading to fallback decision path.
SRE reproduced locally by simulating probe rewrite and observed router flip to fallback when pin replay did not occur before health confirmation timeout.
Confirmed that fallback routing is functioning as designed; root cause is loss of pin signal at probe/edge boundary, not serving runtime mismatch.
resolution:
Applied a two-part mitigation: (1) Hotpatch to edge-proxy config to preserve X-Model-Pin and other custom routing headers on probe handshakes in prod-us-east and eu-west; (2) Increased pin reassertion TTL for enterprise tenants during canary windows and added a router guard to prefer explicit pin cookie over temporary probe-unhealthy flag for up to 60s if cookie is present. Deployed targeted reassert for Finlytics sessions.

Follow-up actions: create a control-plane check that treats explicit pin cookie as authoritative unless explicit unpin command is received; add automated pre-canary checklist to ensure probe header pass-through; update runbook and notify customer.
